title: Affinity for Technology Interaction in Robotic Inner Ear Surgery Processes
summary:
We would like to find out what people with cochlear implants (CIs) and ear, nose, and throat (ENT) specialists think about robotic surgery. In this study, we are exploring whether people who enjoy using new technology are more likely to choose a fully motorized surgical procedure (HEARO® or OTODRIVE®). These systems are often referred to as robotic techniques in surgery.

How does the study work?
The study takes place at several hospitals. We invite both patients and doctors to take part in an online survey. In this survey, we ask questions about how you use technology in everyday life and what you think about robotic surgery.

Why is this study important?
By taking part, you can help us make cochlear implant care better suited to the needs of patients. The results will help us improve robotic surgical procedures and explain them more clearly to patients and professionals.

What is the goal of the study?
The study aims to improve care for people with cochlear implants. We also want to learn more about how patients and doctors understand and evaluate new surgical technologies.
conditions: Presence of otological and audiological implants

interventions.name: Patients who have undergone robotic cochlear implantation using HEARO® and/or OTODRIVE® will be surveyed.

Patients who meet the inclusion criteria for robotic cochlear implantation with HEARO® and/or OTODRIVE® but have opted against this procedure and instead received a conventional cochlear implantation will be surveyed.
Surgeons who have performed robotic cochlear implantation using HEARO® and/or OTODRIVE® will be surveyed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Group A (Robotic Cochlear Implantation)
The patient has received a cochlear implant and underwent surgery using the HEARO® and/or OTODRIVE® robotic surgical technique.
The patient is at least 18 years of age.
The patient has sufficient language proficiency in the language spoken at the implanting clinic and in which the questionnaire is administered (at least B1 level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages [CEFR]).
Group B (Conventional Cochlear Implantation)
The patient has received a cochlear implant and did not undergo surgery using the HEARO® and/or OTODRIVE® surgical technique.
The patient is at least 18 years of age.
The patient has sufficient language proficiency in the language spoken at the implanting clinic and in which the questionnaire is administered (at least B1 level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages [CEFR]).
Group C (Surgeon Group)
The surgeon has performed at least one cochlear implantation using the HEARO® and/or OTODRIVE® surgical technique.
The surgeon has sufficient language proficiency in the language spoken at the clinic and in which the questionnaire is administered (at least B1 level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages [CEFR]).
Exclusion criteria:
Group A (Robotic Cochlear Implantation)
The patient does not meet the inclusion criteria listed above.
The patient has insufficient language proficiency in the language of the questionnaire.
The patient has a diagnosed psychiatric disorder that may bias or distort the accuracy of the provided information.
Group B (Conventional Cochlear Implantation)
The patient does not meet the inclusion criteria listed above.
The patient has insufficient language proficiency in the language of the questionnaire.
The patient has a diagnosed psychiatric disorder that may bias or distort the accuracy of the provided information.
Group C (Surgeon Group)
The surgeon has insufficient language proficiency in the language of the questionnaire.
